name: Mobile ALOHA
summary: Mobile ALOHA adds a mobile base with whole-body teleoperation, letting one operator command base and both arms simultaneously. The headline result is empirical: co-training the mobile policy with the existing static ALOHA dataset lifts success by up to 90% on tasks with only 50 mobile demonstrations, covering cooking shrimp, calling and riding an elevator, and wiping spills.
innovation: Whole-body teleoperation interface making mobile bimanual collection practical for one person.
Static/mobile co-training as a data-efficiency multiplier.
matters: Its widely shared demos shifted public and investor expectations of home robots.
limits: Task-specific policies; each new task still needs its own demonstrations.
lineage: ACT extended to a mobile base with whole-body teleoperation.
